title: Microsoft Teams: shared call history in the Queues app on mobile
summary: The briefing's rollout, licensing, default state and controls are supported by the supplied Microsoft notice and the Microsoft documentation read in this check. The documentation still gives conflicting locations for template assignment, which the briefing explicitly reports.

claims.where: controls[0].governs; Risk assessment: Data exposure; Scope; Governance controls
claims.claim: A Shared Call History template decides which types of queue history are available and who can see them.
claims.quote: A Shared Call History template defines the type of call queue history that's available and who can see it.

claims.claim: IncomingMissedCalls accepts None, AuthorizedUsersOnly and AuthorizedUsersAndAgents.
claims.quote:
### -IncomingMissedCalls
Who sees Call Queue incoming missed calls and shared voicemails in the shared call history.
Supported values: None | AuthorizedUsersOnly | AuthorizedUsersAndAgents

claims.claim: AnsweredAndOutboundCalls accepts None, AuthorizedUsersOnly and AuthorizedUsersAndAgents.
claims.quote:
### -AnsweredAndOutboundCalls
Who sees Call Queue answered and outbound calls in the shared call history.
Supported values: None | AuthorizedUsersOnly | AuthorizedUsersAndAgents

claims.claim: AuthorizedUsersAndAgents permits agents as well as authorized users to see that category.
claims.quote: This example creates a new Shared Call History template where incoming missed calls for Call Queue are shown to authorized users and agents and, answered and outbound calls are shown to authorized users only.

claims.claim: Teams admin center > Voice > Templates and resources > Templates > Shared call history > Add > Incoming missed calls permission reaches the template control.
claims.quote:
go to Voice > Templates and resources.
Select Templates.
Select Shared call history as the template type.
Select Add to create a new Shared Call History template.
Select the appropriate Incoming missed calls permission level.

claims.claim: New-CsSharedCallHistoryTemplate -Name <String> -Description <String> -IncomingMissedCalls AuthorizedUsersAndAgents -AnsweredAndOutboundCalls AuthorizedUsersOnly creates the described MicrosoftTeams template.
claims.quote: New-CsSharedCallHistoryTemplate -Name "Customer Service" -Description "Missed:All Answered:Auth" -IncomingMissedCalls AuthorizedUsersAndAgents -AnsweredAndOutboundCalls AuthorizedUsersOnly

claims.claim: The template form also sets Answered and outbound calls permission.
claims.quote:
Select the appropriate Incoming missed calls permission level.
Select the appropriate Answered and outbound calls permission level.

claims.claim: The cited setup instructions give Teams admin center > Voice > Call queues > call queue > General info > Shared call history template for assignment.
claims.quote:
go to Voice > Call queues.
Select the call queue you want to have shared call history for.
On the General info tab, scroll to find the Shared call history template section.
Select the appropriate Shared Call History template from the dropdown.

claims.claim: MicrosoftTeams Set-CsCallQueue -Identity <Guid> -SharedCallQueueHistoryTemplateId <String> applies a Shared Call History template to the queue.
claims.quote:
Set-CsCallQueue
    -Identity <Guid>
    [-SharedCallQueueHistoryTemplateId <String>]
The SharedCallQueueHistoryTemplateId parameter indicates the Shared Call History template to apply to the call queue.

claims.claim: Conference mode must be enabled, with -ConferenceMode set to $true, for shared call history template assignment to apply.
claims.quote:
### -SharedCallQueueHistoryTemplateId
The SharedCallQueueHistoryTemplateId parameter indicates the Shared Call History template to apply to the call queue.
Note
`-ConferenceMode` must be set to $true

claims.claim: Set-CsCallQueue's reference says shared call history is unavailable when a Teams channel supplies queue membership.
claims.quote:
Shared call history is not availble when using a Teams channel for queue membership
- `-ChannelId` and `-ChannelUserObjectId` are set.

claims.claim: The setup page's August 17, 2026 change log says assigning templates moved to the new Templates step.
claims.quote:
August 17, 2026
- Assigning templates to a call queue has moved to the new Templates step.

claims.claim: The main call queue setup guide places shared-call-history template selection in Templates rather than General info.
claims.quote:
#### Step 7: Templates
##### Set the Shared call history for call queue template (optional)
Select an existing template from the dropdown or Create a new template.

claims.claim: Learn lists iOS and Android mobile clients as supporting the Queues app.
claims.quote: The Queues app is currently supported on Teams desktop, Mac, and Virtualized Desktop Infrastructure (VDI) clients, Teams phones (touch devices only), and iOS and Android mobile clients.

claims.claim: Users must be in at least one call queue to use the Queues app.
claims.quote: In order to use Queues app, your users must be in at least one Call queue.

claims.claim: Supervisor access is based on authorized-user setup as well as the template permissions.
claims.quote: Admins can now delegate authorized users, also known as leads or supervisors, to manage and configure Call queues and Auto attendants directly from the Teams client.

claims.claim: Teams admin center > Teams apps > Manage apps > Actions > Org-wide app settings > Microsoft apps > Off turns off the Queues app org-wide.
claims.quote: You can turn off the Queues app via the Teams admin center. ... Navigate to Teams apps > Manage apps. Select Actions > Org-wide app settings > Microsoft apps. Select Off and Save.

claims.claim: Turning off the Queues app using that org-wide Microsoft apps setting also turns off other Microsoft apps such as Insights and Tasks.
claims.quote: You can turn off the Queues app via the Teams admin center. However, doing so also turns off other Microsoft apps like Insights and Tasks.

claims.claim: Learn's planning page gives the shared-call-history window as the last 3,000 entries or 6 months of calls per call queue, without the briefing asserting a separate mobile guarantee.
claims.quote: Shared Call History shows the last 3,000 entries, or 6 months of calls, per voice application.

claims.claim: The notice names no new identity or permission model for mobile beyond the existing administrative settings.
claims.quote: Searched: Microsoft Teams Queues app mobile shared call history identity permissions. Read MC1556098 in full and manage-queues-app, shared-history setup and template reference; the notice says mobile uses the same administrative settings and introduces no separate identity model.
